This process involves the use of four different nucleotides (A, C, G, and T) to create a new strand that is complementary to the original template. The chain termination method used in this technique involves the addition of a special base called a 'dideoxynucleotide' or 'ddNTP'. This ddNTP is added to the growing chain at a specific point, causing the chain to terminate at that point. In the Sanger dideoxy sequencing technique, the ddNTPs are added to the reaction mixture in four separate tubes, each containing one of the four normal deoxynucleotides (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, and dTTP). The ddNTPs are then allowed to react with the growing chains, causing the chains to terminate at specific points. The newly formed peptide bond is then fixed and stabilized by a conformational change in the peptidyl transferase center, which results in the formation of a new ester bond between the 3' OH group of the tRNA in the P site and the 2'-OH group of the A-site tRNA. The completion of the peptidyl transfer reaction causes the A- and P-site tRNAs to dissociate from the ribosome. 7.
